evals.prompt: Turn this deploy checklist that I keep pasting into chats into a reusable skill.
evals.expected_output: A new skill scaffold with a retrieval-oriented description, validated.
expectations: The skill-creator skill was activated
Trigger phrases and the expected output format are captured before writing
The folder name is kebab-case and matches the name field in the frontmatter
The description states what the skill does, when to use it and a negative boundary, within 1,024 characters
The skill is validated with the bundled validation script

evals.prompt: I wrote a skill for reviewing database migrations but it never loads when I ask about migrations. Fix that.
evals.expected_output: An undertriggering fix made in the description.
expectations: The skill-creator skill was activated
Trigger phrases and technical keywords users would actually say are added to the description
The revised description stays within the length limit and has no angle brackets

evals.prompt: Two of my skills keep firing on the same prompts and I get both of them loaded. Sort that out.
evals.expected_output: An overlap resolution by redrawing the boundary or merging.
expectations: The skill-creator skill was activated
A negative boundary naming the owning skill is added to each description
The overlap is resolved by redrawing the boundary or merging, and each 'use Y instead' is mirrored by the other skill

evals.prompt: Write test cases for my skill so I can tell whether it triggers properly.
evals.expected_output: An evals file with positive and near-miss negative cases in the house schema.
expectations: The skill-creator skill was activated
The output is evals/evals.json with a skill_name and evals entries that each hold an id, prompt, expected_output and expectations
Negative cases are near-misses from an adjacent skill rather than obviously unrelated prompts

evals.prompt: Review this skill folder before I publish it and tell me what is wrong with it.
evals.expected_output: A structural and content audit against the review checklist.
expectations: The skill-creator skill was activated
The file is named SKILL.md exactly and the folder name matches the name field
SKILL.md length, a README inside the folder and the description's what-and-when content are checked

evals.prompt: Split this large feature into tasks for parallel agents and pick which installed skill each task should use.
evals.expected_output: Task decomposition and skill routing, not skill authoring.
expectations: The skill-creator skill was NOT activated
The planner skill was activated

evals.prompt: Write the design document and the release notes for our project.
expectations: The skill-creator skill was NOT activated
The work-docs skill was activated

evals.prompt: Review the helper script in my pull request for correctness and naming.
evals.expected_output: A code review of ordinary code, not a skill audit.
expectations: The skill-creator skill was NOT activated
The code-review skill was activated
